title: The 20-Watt Computer: How the Brain Computes. A Quantitative Approach for Engineers
description:
A free textbook that treats the brain as an engineer would treat a machine: circuits, signals, codes, control loops, learning rules and energy budgets. Neuron types are named by what they put on the wire (GLUT, GABA, DOPA, SERO, NORA, ACET). Every number in the book comes from a small Python model that can be run and changed, and every major claim is traced to its experiment in an experimental supplement.

Editions in English, Chinese, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Japanese, Korean, Vietnamese, Arabic, Russian and Ukrainian, each with a full book (22 chapters, about 160 exercises with answers, about 370 checked references) and a pocket-size paperback without formulas. Website with an online reader and an interactive neuron breadboard: https://kladkogex.github.io/20-watt-computer/
notes: Text, figures and exercises: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Code (models, build scripts, breadboard): MIT.
